hypotheses.justification: `hsm` follows from `coordinate_apply`, and the conclusion `BrownianWickPurePowerMixedInnerIdentity hB` does not mention it; it is only passed along in the proof. From `coordinate_apply` we get `B t = ⇑(coordinate t)` by `funext (coordinate_apply t)`. Since `coordinate t : StrongDual ℝ W` is a continuous linear map, `(coordinate t).continuous.stronglyMeasurable` applies. Mathlib's `Continuous.stronglyMeasurable` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/StronglyMeasurable/Basic.lean:723) needs `[OpensMeasurableSpace W]`, which comes from the variable `[BorelSpace W]`, a pseudo-metrizable target (ℝ), and `SecondCountableTopologyEither W ℝ`, which holds because ℝ is second countable. The argument works for every t, so there is no degenerate case. New proof: `have hsm : ∀ t, StronglyMeasurable (B t) := fun t => by rw [show B t = ⇑(coordinate t) from funext (coordinate_apply t)]; exact (coordinate t).continuous.stronglyMeasurable`, then keep the existing proof term. `generated` would also work: `IsWienerGenerated.measurable` makes each `B t` measurable, and a measurable real-valued function is strongly measurable.
